entries.proposition: WWOX is one of the three commonest autosomal-recessive genes in the cohort, with two diagnosed patients.
entries.snippet: In the AR inheritance model, AP4M1 (n = 3), TBC1D23 (n = 2), and WWOX (n = 2) were the most frequently encountered genes.

entries.proposition: The Table 2 footnote defines R as the 12 patients whose diagnosis informed therapy.
entries.snippet: Cases marked with ‘R’ include the 12 patients in whom genetic diagnosis directly informed therapeutic decisions

entries.proposition: Section 3.5 names the 12 therapy-informed patients as SCN1A, SLC2A1 and MECP2 carriers and redefines R as drug resistance.
entries.snippet: In 12 of 89 diagnosed patients (13.5%), genetic results directly informed therapeutic decisions: (1) SCN1A‐positive cases (n = 9) avoided sodium channel blockers (e.g., carbamazepine, lamotrigine) to reduce seizure exacerbation risk; (2) SLC2A1 variants (n = 2) prompted ketogenic diet trials with subsequent seizure reduction; (3) MECP2 diagnosis (n = 1) enabled Rett syndrome‐specific surveillance including scoliosis monitoring and cardiac screening. Of these 12 patients, 6 were drug‐resistant (indicated with ‘R’ in Table 2)
entries.anchor: Results, Clinical utility of genetic diagnosis

entries.proposition: Table 2 is a partial listing whose stated totals differ from the text.
entries.snippet: Full table includes all 98 P/LP and 47 clinically relevant VUS cases; only representative entries shown.
Functional validation (e.g., electrophysiology for SCN1A variants) was not performed.
